purpose: silver_ourairports_airports is the cleaned, one-row-per-airport reference table built from bronze.ourairports_airports (9057 rows). It carries airport identity (id, ident, iata_code, icao_code, gps_code, local_code), classification (type, has_scheduled_service), geography (latitude_deg, longitude_deg, elevation_ft, continent, iso_country, iso_region, municipality) and reference links, and feeds downstream joins that attribute flights, routes or traffic metrics to an airport.
usage: Join on id (the declared grain) or on ident when matching external OurAirports extracts; iata_code and icao_code are the usual join keys against carrier data but icao_code is null for 1237 rows (13.7%) so use an outer join or filter deliberately. has_scheduled_service is a boolean derived from the bronze 'yes'/'no' text and is the intended filter for commercial-service airports. latitude_deg and longitude_deg are decimal degrees suitable for distance maths; elevation_ft is whole feet and may be negative (min -1266).
limitations: Capture metadata (_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, _airbyte_meta) is excluded, so this table carries no load lineage or extraction timestamp. Several columns are sparsely populated and were retained as-is rather than cleaned or imputed: local_code (null_rate 0.636635), keywords (0.679585), home_link (0.749034), wikipedia_link (0.130838), icao_code (0.136579), gps_code (0.053881), municipality (0.039748) and elevation_ft (0.036988). keywords remains an unparsed free-text list, and the external URLs in home_link and wikipedia_link are not validated. The id and elevation_ft casts rest on the 10 sampled values per column plus the reported min/max, so a reviewer should confirm them against the full warehouse table before approval.
